Subject: Pilot pricing and deployment options for inference (hosted vs dedicated vs private)

Hi Oliver — great to meet earlier. Quick recap and three concrete pricing paths so we can align on a pilot and next steps.

Key takeaways from the demo call:
- Workload: product search re-ranker + short personalized responses (average prompt ~120 tokens, expected 0.5–1.5M prompts/day at peak).
- Latency goal: p95 <= 150ms for the re-ranker in production windows (US).
- Security: must support private VPC for PII-sensitive flows; willing to pilot on Hosted if we can set strong controls.

Three deployment paths (high level):
1) Hosted API (pay-as-you-go) — fastest to start, no infra commit, per-token pricing + optional reserved commit credit. Good if traffic is spiky.
2) Dedicated (reserved GPU capacity) — monthly/annual committed pool; predictable throughput and lower unit costs for sustained volume.
3) Private (VPC / on-prem) — for strict security/regulatory needs; includes private control plane and optional on-prem package.

Quick ask from our side to model costs: can you confirm typical concurrent requests during peak search windows and whether burst capacity (x2) is required on promotional days? Also confirm SSO/legal contact so we can push a short SLA/POC doc.

Attached: brief cost model template (we'll fill once you confirm concurrency).

Proposed next steps:
- You confirm concurrency & whether private VPC is a must for pilot (reply inline).
- We send a tailored cost worksheet + pilot proposal (2–4 week pilot suggestion) and draft SLA.
- If you prefer Dedicated, we'll provide three SKU/commit options and a 3-month pilot discount.

Thanks — Marcus

Oliver — thanks for the details. I filled a short cost sketch below and attached a spreadsheet (stellar_cost_model_v1.xlsx) with line-item math. High level numbers are conservative — we can tighten after you share actual concurrency over peak windows.

Summary (ballpark, USD):
- Hosted (pay-as-you-go): $0.0008 per token for generation-like flows; for a re-ranker pattern assume ~100 tokens consumed per request on average. With 2M prompts/day that maps to ~200M tokens/day -> ~ $160k/day (this is illustrative; we can apply tiered discounts and reserved credit). For a 4-week pilot this is often costly without reserved credit — we usually propose a time-bound pilot credit or temporary commit.

- Dedicated (reserved capacity): multiple SKU options. Example: a medium reserved pool sized to handle steady 1.2M prompts/day with burst headroom (~2x) runs ~ $45k–$60k/month depending on GPU family and quantization profile. This yields ~3–4x lower unit cost vs Hosted at scale in most of our benchmarks. We can propose a 3-month reserved commit with one-time pilot discount (see proposed line items in attachment).

- Private VPC / On-prem: one-time setup + infra. Typical structure: setup & integration $25k–$50k (one-time), plus monthly infra + support $40k–$80k depending on footprint. Good for regulated PII-sensitive flows where Hosted isn't acceptable.

Recommended pilot path (least friction):
- Option A: 4-week Hosted pilot with $X in pilot credits + audit logging + private network peering where possible. This gets you data quickly with minimal infra work. If acceptable, convert to Dedicated commit after pilot.
- Option B: 3-month Dedicated pilot (small reserved commit) — better economics sooner, requires procurement/PO.

Requested next steps:
1) Oliver: confirm whether you want Hosted pilot with credits or a Dedicated 3-month pilot.
2) If Hosted: we send a pilot credit + short SLA; Security questionnaire goes to Priya (cc'ed) who handles vendor security and will turn around SOC2 artifacts and answers.
3) If Dedicated: we issue a SKU/commit worksheet + draft contract and propose a kickoff.

Attachments: stellar_cost_model_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet with line-item math), redwood_sla_draft.pdf (SLA stub).

Thanks — I can jump on a quick call if you want us to walk the math.

Best,
